source.method: src/utils.cpp: run_mathematical_direction_search, current-word GP-prime-sum totient branch

exact_source_rule: The source sums GP prime values of each visible ciphertext word, takes phi(sum) mod 29, subtracts that shift from its rune indices, and scores the complete page once. It writes a hit if source unigram fitness exceeds 0.85. This is input dependent; applying an opposite shift computed from a proposed plaintext is not in general its inverse.
source_boundary_issue: The source get_words() tokenizes all non-rune separators, but its transformation increments current_word_idx only on SPECIAL_HYPHEN_IDX or SPECIAL_SPACE_IDX. At a period, newline or slash, the word-sum list and clock can differ. Preserve this exact behavior in any future source replay; do not silently repair it.
pretarget_fixture_gate: Under the idealized same-word mapping on the known warning passage, 18 of 50 plaintext words have no ciphertext preimage among the 29 possible uniform word shifts. The first one-rune word already has no preimage; this first-word obstruction does not depend on later delimiter clock behavior. This exploratory gate is not a full source-replay result.
pretarget_fixture_reproduction: python research/source-intake/d4v1_option29_word_gate.py; hashes of the archived alphabet, warning rune page and warning reading are pinned in the script
source_fitness_diagnostic: The original 0.85 rule scores a complete page, not an individual word. A saved 1,000-trial uniform 262-rune diagnostic in experiments/records/d4v1-positional-totient-streams/source-control.json passes 1,000/1,000 at this length. That does not calibrate all source page lengths or any joint positional z gate.
next_work: A source-exact candidate generator must handle input-dependent preimage existence and the actual separator clock, then demonstrate recovery of a complete known-reading plant before treating target absence as a negative. No alternate word rule or output-based inverse has been supplied.
